# A run that ends while a landing is in progress is gathered and landed before the swarm starts a task of lower priority.
# Three P0 tasks and four P3 tasks. Two slots. The P0 tasks a and c write the same file, so c conflicts when it lands, and the swarm files a merge task of priority P0.
# The barrier makes the case happen on every run: task c ends while the batch of a and b lands (the forge waits after its first merge, forge/pause-after-merge, until c is over).
# At the next read of the queue, c is over but not yet gathered, so two slots look free. A swarm that starts tasks then fills both slots with P3 tasks.
# The P3 tasks (a body that starts with late) hold their slots until a merge call is in calls.log, so the merge task would have no slot: the swarm waits on itself.
# The claim is an order: the merge call comes before every late-end line. A task that reaches its deadline writes the file harness-fault, which is a fault of the script and not of the claim.
isolate
swarmfakes

env BATCH=2
exec obeeswarm item add swarm swarm-1 --title 'The swarm' --body-file backlog.txt
exec obeeswarm run swarm-1 swarm --workflow swarm/workflow.star

# No task hit its hang guard.
! exists harness-fault

# The merge task ran once, and it came before every P3 task ended.
grep -count=1 '^resolve ' calls.log
grep -count=4 '^late-end ' calls.log
exec awk '/^resolve / && !r {r = NR} /^late-end / && !l {l = NR} END {exit !(r && l && r < l)}' calls.log

# Everything landed.
grep -count=7 '^MergePR ' forge/calls.log
exec grep -rhao '7 landed, 0 need a person, 0 not started' state

-- forge/pause-after-merge --
swarm-4
-- backlog.txt --
P0	zero-a	a.txt
P0	zero-b	after-start b.txt
P0	zero-c	in-landing a.txt
P3	three-a	late l1.txt
P3	three-b	late l2.txt
P3	three-c	late l3.txt
P3	three-d	late l4.txt
